title: Serving Runtime Consolidated Playbook: Architecture, Scheduling, Profiling, Benchmarks, Release Notes, and Runbooks
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This consolidated playbook documents the serving runtime architecture, kernel and scheduling strategies, profiling procedures, the benchmarking suite, recent release notes, known issues, operational runbooks, and team wiki references. It is intended as the single authoritative reference for on-call engineers, performance engineers, and release owners.

Goals
- Capture architecture and design rationales that affect latency and throughput.
- Standardize kernel selection and scheduling policies across hardware classes.
- Provide a repeatable profiling and perf-regression workflow.
- Define the benchmarking suite and expected baselines.
- Consolidate runbooks for common incidents and operational tasks.

1) Runtime Architecture (summary)
- High-level components:
  - Frontend API (edge proxies + request routing)
  - Smart Router (policy engine; routes by latency/cost/region)
  - Worker Pool (GPU-backed inference processes)
  - KV Cache Layer (prefix and embedding caches)
  - Telemetry & Observability (tracing, per-token metrics, error pipelines)
- Design principles:
  - Keep fast-path lightweight: frontends do minimal validation and auth.
  - Worker isolation by model-variant to ensure predictable memory/KV behavior.
  - Continuous batching with adaptive windows tuned per SLO.
  - Fallback variants: smaller/quantized model routes when capacity constrained.

Architecture diagram (textual)
- Request -> API Proxy -> Smart Router -> Queue -> Worker (GPU instance) -> KV Cache -> Token generation -> Response

Key config knobs (table)
- Model shard size: number of shards per worker (default: "4")
- Batch window ms: batching aggregation window (default: "6ms")
- KV cache TTLs: prefix TTL (default: "120s"), embedding TTL (default: "3600s")
- Fallback policy: on_queue_wait_ms threshold (default: "200ms")

2) Kernel selection and Scheduling
- Kernel tiers:
  - Tier 0: optimized fused attention kernels (NVIDIA H100 / equivalent)
  - Tier 1: mixed optimized kernels (A10/NVIDIA L4)
  - Tier 2: reference kernels (CPU fallback or older GPUs)
- Scheduling policies:
  - Latency-first: prioritize low-latency requests (< 95th percentile target) by dispatching to reserved low-latency pool.
  - Throughput-first: aggregate larger batches with slightly higher latency tolerance.
  - Cost-aware: route to quantized model variants on cost-sensitive tiers.
- Kernel selection heuristic (overview):
  - Match model architecture -> recommended kernel profile.
  - Inspect sequence-length histogram for route -> choose kernel tuned for observed sequence distribution.
  - Prefer fused kernels for transformer blocks when available.

3) Profiling Playbook (for perf engineers and on-call)
- When to profile:
  - Noticeable regressions vs baseline: 10%+ increase in median latency or drop in tokens/sec.
  - New kernel/release or model onboarding.
  - Capacity incidents where queue growth is unexplained.
- Tools and artifacts:
  - Lightweight traces: enable request sampling via /debug/trace (span-level).
  - GPU traces: nvprof / Nsight System configs (capture wall-time, kernel durations, memcpy).
  - Internal flamegraphs: collection via runtime-profiler -> /profiles/{id}.
  - Perf harness: benchctl (see Benchmarking Suite).
- Profiling procedure (step-by-step):
  1. Reproduce on staging with the same model, batch distribution, and input corpus.
  2. Capture API + worker traces (5-10 minutes).
  3. Collect kernel timelines and PCIe memcpy metrics.
  4. Analyze hot kernels (top 3) and identify stalls (e.g., memcpy, synchronization).
  5. Test alternate kernel candidates (Tier 0 vs Tier 1) and compare p50/p95/p99.
  6. If regression persists, open a perf-ticket and include traces + candidate configs.
- Common root causes and mitigations:
  - Memory fragmentation -> restart worker shard (short-term) + schedule compaction (long-term).
  - NVLink saturation -> reduce inter-GPU scatters or increase batch-locality.
  - Bad kernel fallback -> pin kernel version matching release-tested profile.

4) Benchmarking Suite
- Purpose: reproducible baselines for model variants across hardware classes and kernel profiles.
- Tooling: benchctl (CLI) with YAML scenario files. Outputs: tokens/sec, latency distribution, GPU utilization, mem usage.
- Canonical scenarios:
  - Synth short (avg seq 32), synth medium (128), synth long (1024), chat-multi-turn (avg turn 80).
  - Embedding throughput: batch sizes 1,8,32,128.
- Baseline expectations (example, H100):
  - synth short p50 latency: < 4ms/token
  - synth medium throughput: > 12k tokens/sec per GPU
  - chat-multi-turn p95: < 120ms per turn (model-dependent)
- Running the suite (example):
# Run benchctl against staging cluster
benchctl run --scenario chat-multi-turn --cluster staging --model catalog/redwood-7b --out ./bench-results

- Interpreting results: compare against saved baselines in /benchmarks/baseline-YYYYMMDD.csv and track regression PRs if >5% drop in tokens/sec or >10% increase in p95 latency.

5) Release Notes (recent)
- v2026.01.15:
  - Improved fused attention kernel stability on H100; reduced median latency by ~8% for long sequences.
  - Added adaptive batch-window tuning to smart router.
- v2026.02.20:
  - KV cache TTLs made configurable per-customer; fixed eviction bug causing cold-start latency spikes.
  - Benchctl added new chat-multi-turn scenario and CSV exporter.

6) Known Issues and Workarounds
- Issue: Occasional p99 spikes during large model rollouts.
  - Symptoms: sudden increase in p99 for specific model-name, queue depth rises.
  - Cause: Incompatible kernel selected for new shard geometry.
  - Mitigation: Hotfix: set fallback_kernel=stable-v2026-01 on Smart Router for the model; schedule kernel compatibility test.
- Issue: Memory compaction not triggered on long-lived workers -> fragmentation
  - Workaround: drain and recycle worker shards every 72 hours for models with >= 512M params.
- Issue: NVLink saturation on multi-GPU workers with mixed batch locality.
  - Mitigation: enable batch-locality enforcement flag: scheduler.batch_locality = true

7) Runtime Runbooks (operational procedures)
- Runbook: High p99 latency on production
  1. Confirm alerts: check dashboards (p99 latency by model, queue_depth).
  2. Identify impacted model(s) and earliest spike time.
  3. Check worker errors and OOMs: /logs/worker/{id}.
  4. Temporarily route traffic to fallback variant or smaller quantized model.
  5. If root cause is kernel mismatch, set smart-router override to stable kernel profile.
  6. Open incident with perf traces attached and tag oncall/perf.
- Runbook: GPU OOM on worker
  1. Isolate worker and collect /proc/meminfo and runtime logs.
  2. If reproducible, scale down max_batch_size or shard_count for the model.
  3. Restart worker shard; schedule rolling restarts for other shards.
  4. Add ticket to adjust resource allocation in model-serving-config.
- Runbook: Cache stampede (KV misses during deploy)
  1. Detect: large burst of cache miss ratio and increased latency on cold-starts.
  2. Mitigation: enable gradual rollout (canary) and pre-fill cache using warmup job: cache-warm --model <model> --corpus <sample> --parallel 8.

8) Team Wiki & Onboarding Pointers
- Quickstarts:
  - benchctl quickstart: /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/benchctl-quickstart
  - model onboarding checklist: /applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/checklist
- Ownership
  - Runtime Core: runtime-team@redwood.com (primary owners for kernels, scheduling)
  - Performance & Evals: perf-team@redwood.com (benchmarks, regression gating)
  - Oncall: eng-sre rotation (see /eng-sre/oncall roster)

9) Ownership, SLOs and Alerting
- SLOs (serving-runtime):
  - Global p95 latency (short requests): <= 50ms (SLO target)
  - Error rate (5xx): <= 0.5% per 30d window
  - Queue wait time p95: <= 200ms for latency-class traffic
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - p95 latency breach (5m sustained over SLO): page oncall and notify perf-team.
  - Tokens/sec drop > 15% vs baseline (10m window): create perf-ticket and notify owners.

Appendix: Useful Commands and Snippets
- List top kernels in use (example):
# query internal telemetry service
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://telemetry.internal/api/kernels/top

- Restart worker shard
# drain and restart shard
ctl worker drain --shard-id shard-123
ctl worker restart --shard-id shard-123

- Capture a perf profile (short):
benchctl profile --model redwood-7b --duration 60 --out /tmp/profile-$(date +%s).tar

Document maintenance
- Owner: runtime-core (runtime-team@redwood.com).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major kernel/release change.
- Add new known issues, release notes, and benchmarking baselines to the canonical folders: /benchmarks and /releases.

If you find missing procedures or a new recurring incident pattern, please update this doc and notify reviewers.
